title: "Win + M" shortcut doesn't work after I remap Win -> Alt and Alt -> Win

status.label: Revalidate swapped Win and Alt behavior
status.detail: A maintainer reproduced Win+M failing under the bidirectional Win/Alt swap; the report also documents pen-generated Win+F18–F20 shortcuts being seen as Alt.

judgment.rationale: The maintainer reproduced physical Alt+M failing to invoke Win+M when Win and Alt are swapped, while a direct Alt+M-to-Win+M shortcut works. The reporter also described Win+W and pen-generated Win+F18–F20 behavior and supplied a bug report. The issue is old, so current engine behavior should be reproduced before finalizing the affected state path.
evidence: A maintainer reproduced the Win+M failure with Win(left) and Alt(left) remapped to each other.
The maintainer reported that a direct Alt+M-to-Win+M shortcut mapping works around the Win+M failure.
The reporter described Win+W opening Game Bar and pen-generated Win+F18–F20 shortcuts being observed as Alt combinations.
A report archive was attached in 2022; no later discussion adds a current-version confirmation.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the bidirectional modifier swap on current stable and verify whether physical-to-logical modifier state is handled consistently for shell shortcuts and synthetic device shortcuts.

fix_assessment.rationale: The maintainer reproduction and direct-shortcut workaround support investigating how single-key modifier swaps compose with shell- and device-generated chords. The exact state boundary needs current-code confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Track physical and remapped modifier state consistently
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The bidirectional Win/Alt swap may leave shell-handled or synthetic-device chords using the physical modifier identity instead of the remapped logical identity; current event flow must be verified.
plan: Reproduce Win+M, Win+W, and pen Win+F18–F20 behavior with Win(left)↔Alt(left) on current stable.
Trace the physical modifier down/up events and the logical events emitted to shell shortcuts and synthetic devices.
If modifier identity diverges, track the remapped logical modifier through matching key-up and reset paths without changing standalone key behavior.
Add engine regression tests for the bidirectional swap, direct shortcut workaround, and injected device chords.
verification: Physical Alt+M invokes Win+M under the configured bidirectional swap.
Win+W and available pen-generated Win+F18–F20 chords use the configured logical modifier.
All modifiers return to released state and standalone Win continues to open Start.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer reproduced a concrete failure and documented workarounds, but the report predates current engine changes and no current event trace identifies the state boundary.

issue_context.summary: Swapping Win and Alt can break shell shortcuts and synthetic device shortcuts that use the remapped modifier.
known_information: The reporter uses a Mac-layout Logitech keyboard and swaps Win(left) and Alt(left).
A maintainer reproduced Win+M failing under the swap while a direct Alt+M-to-Win+M shortcut works.
The reporter documented Win+W and pen-generated Win+F18–F20 cases and attached a report archive.
inferences: Some shell- or device-generated chords may not observe the logical modifier produced by the single-key remap.
issue_context.analysis: The workaround shows direct chord injection can succeed while the single-key swap fails to compose consistently with other shortcuts. The issue's age makes current reproduction important before committing to a state-management change.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all seven comments; the thread includes a maintainer reproduction, the direct shortcut workaround, additional device shortcuts, and a report archive.
Reviewed the existing schema-v5 artifact and retained its separate physical/logical modifier hypothesis while refreshing the covered source timestamp.
No linked fix or confirmed duplicate appears in the issue discussion.

information_gaps.information: Whether the Win/Alt swap still causes the reported failures on current stable and which of Win+M, Win+W, and pen Win+F18–F20 remains reproducible
information_gaps.why_needed: The maintainer reproduction is from 2022; current behavior determines whether the proposed modifier-state work is still needed and which event paths matter.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the current PowerToys version and report which of the documented shortcuts fail with Win(left) and Alt(left) swapped.

actions.label: Confirm current Win and Alt swap behavior

comment.body: A maintainer reproduced Win+M failing with Win(left) and Alt(left) swapped, and your report also mentions Win+W and pen shortcuts. Could you confirm whether these still fail on current stable and which of those cases you can reproduce?

reproduce.title: Verify logical modifier composition after Win/Alt swap
prerequisites: Configure Win(left) to Alt(left) and Alt(left) to Win(left)
Open ordinary desktop windows; a pen that emits Win+F18–F20 is optional
steps: Press physical Alt(left)+M and check whether all windows minimize.
Press physical Win(left)+W and record the shortcut behavior.
If available, trigger pen-generated Win+F18–F20 shortcuts.
Release all keys and check that no modifier remains active.
reproduce.expected_result: Each chord uses the configured remapped logical modifier, and every key returns to released state.
